newsitem.title: JAPAN: NKK seen resuming dividend payments - paper.
newsitem.headline: NKK seen resuming dividend payments - paper.

text.p: NKK Corp is expected to resume dividend payments for the current year to March 31, 1997, helped by a rise in income and higher profits in its heavy industry business, a Japanese daily said on Wednesday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun economic daily said that NKK is likely to pay a three yen annual dividend for 1996/97.
NKK has not paid dividends since 1993/94 because of poor business performance stemming from an overall slump in the Japanese economy.
The company is also expected to erase accumulated losses of 42 billion yen in 1996/97, the paper said.
A spokesmen for NKK was not immediately available for comment.
Last week NKK said that it plans to sell some of the land it owns for about 20 billion yen during 1996/97. It declined to comment on its net profit forecast for 1996/97.
In September, the company lowered its parent current profit forecast for the year to 40 billion yen from its May forecast of 45 billion yen.
In 1995/96, NKK posted a parent current profit of 30.32 billion yen and a net profit of 59.75 billion yen.
